title: Linear-time prefixing with bounded space
statement: For every Boolean word $w$, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $c$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the concatenation $w x$. Moreover, for every Boolean word $x$ and every time $t$, the computation of $M$ on $x$ up to time $t$ uses at most $c$ work-tape cells.
